advisories.finding: NT-7 and NT-8 both open their pass condition with 'Refused.' for properties whose actor is the host itself. NT-7's input is 'A host path that derives fail or warn other than from the core policyOutcome'; NT-8's is 'A host path that mints a D9 class, exit number, or HostTermination'. Nothing external refuses a host's own code path, so the verb has no actor. The artifact already shows the right idiom for exactly this shape: NT-6, whose subject is a consumer's mislabelling rather than a refusable request, reads 'The contract forbids that label. No silent promotion.' The four earlier uses of 'Refused' — NT-1, NT-2, NT-4 and NT-5 — are all coherent because each refuses a request or a component payload, so the mismatch is confined to the two new classes.
advisories.whyNotShouldFix: The coverage my v1 finding asked for is real rather than nominal. Each pass condition's substantive clauses state a correct and testable conformance property — the only policy result is core-evaluated policyOutcome, the host maps only existing D9 v1.14 classes, and policyOutcome is not HostTermination — so an implementer can exercise both classes by asserting verdict provenance and D9 provenance. Only the leading verb is mismatched. I grade this as I graded the analogous wording imprecision in the DR-117 chain, where the substance was right and only the phrasing inverted.
advisories.suggestion: Either restate both in NT-6's idiom — an implementation that derives fail or warn outside policyOutcome, or mints a D9 class from it, fails this class — or scope the inputs to a request or configuration that asks the host to apply a threshold outside the core, which would make refusal at admission the coherent outcome. The second reading may be what was intended; the class should say which.

coordinatorSummary: ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX, with 1 non-blocking advisory. Fourteen attacks run, one landed at advisory grade. Custody is intact: subject 081ff7fb at 0444 unmoved and valid JSON, predecessor v1 frozen at ba2a0a68, HEAD never left f5094f0, file 08 and COORD at their pins with a clean tree. Both of my v1 findings are repaired and I tested each from the bytes rather than the disposition table. The prohibition-to-class map rebuilt from the artifact now shows 3 of 3 covered — NT-7 for the fail/warn verdict, NT-8 for the D9 code and HostTermination, with NT-8 broader than the prohibition since it also names exit number and the pack-threshold path — against 0 of 3 at v1. The D-078 clause is restored and I confirmed it is present verbatim in D-078's Decision, singular 'wait' included. My venue-elsewhere advisory is correctly ROUTED rather than performed, and Codex's advisory is declined inside its own framing, which is the right way to close a non-blocking finding one does not adopt. The roster carries all four v1 items from both reviewers with dispositions and pointers, the most complete in the three contract chains for this goal. The normalised diff confirms the revision is minimal, and I re-verified the row quote and the nine-fragment cell reconstruction against live file 08 rather than trusting that. The one advisory is that NT-7 and NT-8 open their pass condition with 'Refused.' for properties whose actor is the host itself, where nothing external refuses a host's own code path — the artifact's own NT-6 shows the correct conformance idiom for that shape. I pressed hardest here because the corpus has twice returned sibling contracts for pass properties naming an impossible mechanism and because I cleared exactly that defect wrongly at DR-117 v3, but this is not that: both pass conditions' substantive clauses state correct and testable properties, so the coverage is real and only the verb is mismatched. This acceptance is of the artifact as an independently reviewed design-contract candidate only; it applies nothing, marks no row SATISFIED, opens no D-056 class, and executes no class.
